CLOCK_PERIOD.meaning: Clock period in ns; sets create_clock in every SDC (and is passed to ABC as -D).
CLOCK_PERIOD.safe: Tighten only (lower than the config value). Repo rule: 25 ns is the committed value and may never be raised.
CLOCK_PERIOD.symptom: Lower it to find the speed margin: setup slack shrinks one for one. A negative setup slack at a tighter period only means the experiment does not fit; the committed 25 ns stays.
CLOCK_PERIOD.verify: build/whatif/<d>__<tag>/runs/<tag>/final/metrics.json (whatif_result), designs/<d>/output/reports/timing_summary.rpt for the committed run: timing__setup__ws per corner
CLOCK_PERIOD.repo: 25 in every committed design (40 MHz on wb_clk_i)

MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Max slew (ns) set by set_max_transition in the SDC and used by synthesis buffering and CTS.
MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT.safe: Tighten only (lower than the effective value, PDK default 0.75 ns). The wrapper configs carry 1.5 for the Caravel top; never raise a macro past 0.75.
MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT.symptom: Lowering it makes repair work harder and raises cell count; it exposes which nets are near the limit. Raising it is how a slew gate is cheated: forbidden.
MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT.verify: metrics.json design__max_slew_violation__count and timing_summary.rpt Max Slew column
MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT.repo: 0.75 ns PDK default in the macros (not set in their config.json); 1.5 only in the three user_project_wrapper* configs

MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Max fanout set by set_max_fanout; drives synthesis buffering (ABC buffer -N) and repair_design.
MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT.safe: Tighten only (lower). Repo uses 8 (user_proj_example 16 from the template); the PDK default is 10.
MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT.symptom: High-fanout nets with large slew or cap violations; lowering adds buffers.

MAX_CAPACITANCE_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Max capacitance (pF) set by set_max_capacitance when provided; unset means the library limit applies.
MAX_CAPACITANCE_CONSTRAINT.safe: Tighten only. Leave unset unless a cap violation list points at it.

CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Clock uncertainty (ns) in LibreLane's base.sdc and in the template SDCs (via the SYNTH_CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY alias). Only used by designs that load base.sdc or a SDC reading it.
CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY_CONSTRAINT.safe: Increase only (more margin = tighter). PDK default 0.25 ns.
CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY_CONSTRAINT.symptom: Used to test how much setup/hold margin a path really has.

TIME_DERATING_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Early/late derating in percent applied to all path delays by base.sdc (set_timing_derate).
TIME_DERATING_CONSTRAINT.symptom: Margin experiment on setup and hold together.

IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT.meaning: Input and output delay as a percentage of CLOCK_PERIOD in base.sdc (default 20). Ignored when a design supplies its own SDC (soc_*, tiny_ai_core, user_proj_example, wrappers).
IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT.safe: Increase only (less time left inside the block).
IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT.symptom: Setup slack on in-to-reg and reg-to-out paths.

OUTPUT_CAP_LOAD.meaning: Capacitive load (fF) on every output port in base.sdc (set_load).
OUTPUT_CAP_LOAD.symptom: Output-driver slew and timing under a heavier load.

SYNTH_STRATEGY.meaning: ABC script for logic synthesis and mapping. AREA 0: resyn2 then amap. AREA 1: adds a choice2 area-recovery pass. AREA 2: choice2 twice. AREA 3: the OpenROAD-flow-scripts area script (map -B 0.9, buffer/upsize/dnsize with MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT). DELAY 0..4 are speed-oriented and FORBIDDEN here.
SYNTH_STRATEGY.safe: AREA 0, AREA 1, AREA 2, AREA 3. Never any DELAY value.
SYNTH_STRATEGY.symptom: Cell count / area too high, or a path too long: try the next AREA value and compare cells, area and slack. AREA 3 often bigger (LibreLane's own explore table: 11620 vs about 6700 cells on its sample).
SYNTH_STRATEGY.verify: synth_stat.rpt in the run dir (06-yosys-synthesis/reports/stat.rpt) and metrics.json design__instance__count__stdcell
SYNTH_STRATEGY.doc: LibreLane step -> engine table (Yosys + ABC are outside OpenROAD); .claude/skills/tune-synthesis/reference.md

SYNTH_SIZING.meaning: ABC upsize/dnsize pass after mapping (instead of buffering).
SYNTH_SIZING.symptom: Weak drivers on slow paths; costs area.
SYNTH_SIZING.doc: LibreLane step -> engine table (Yosys + ABC are outside OpenROAD); .claude/skills/tune-synthesis/reference.md

SYNTH_ABC_BUFFERING.meaning: ABC buffer -N <max fanout> [-S max slew] + upsize + dnsize (alias SYNTH_BUFFERING).
SYNTH_ABC_BUFFERING.symptom: Fanout/slew violations already present at synthesis.
SYNTH_ABC_BUFFERING.doc: LibreLane step -> engine table (Yosys + ABC are outside OpenROAD); .claude/skills/tune-synthesis/reference.md

SYNTH_DIRECT_WIRE_BUFFERING.meaning: Inserts a buffer on wires that connect an input directly to an output (feed-throughs).
SYNTH_DIRECT_WIRE_BUFFERING.safe: Leave true; false can give assign statements, which the netlist check rejects.
SYNTH_DIRECT_WIRE_BUFFERING.doc: LibreLane step -> engine table (Yosys + ABC are outside OpenROAD); .claude/skills/tune-synthesis/reference.md

SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE.meaning: flatten (default), deferred_flatten, keep. Flattening lets ABC optimise across modules.
SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE.safe: flatten or deferred_flatten for the committed style; keep only to study a block.
SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE.symptom: Cannot see which block dominates area: keep (with SYNTH_KEEP_HIERARCHY_*) shows per-module cells in synth_stat.rpt.

FP_SIZING.meaning: absolute: the die comes from DIE_AREA; relative: from FP_CORE_UTIL and FP_ASPECT_RATIO.
FP_SIZING.symptom: Switching to relative lets the core follow the cell area.

DIE_AREA.meaning: Die rectangle x0 y0 x1 y1 in um (absolute sizing).
DIE_AREA.safe: Size for 40 percent utilisation; 80 x 80 um is the smallest committed die (vision_block, 60 percent). Utilisation above about 80 percent failed (GPL / repair OOM). Wrapper DIE_AREA is fixed geometry: not editable.
DIE_AREA.symptom: GPL-0301 'cannot place' or repair out of memory: the die is too small. Utilisation far under 30 percent wastes area.
DIE_AREA.repo: 80x80 for tiny engines, 120 (prec_int8, image_text_match), 170..340 for the larger ones; see each //DIE_AREA comment

FP_CORE_UTIL.meaning: Core utilisation percent (relative sizing only); also the base of the default placement density.
FP_CORE_UTIL.symptom: Default PL target density = FP_CORE_UTIL + 5 * GPL_CELL_PADDING + 10.

FP_PRUNE_THRESHOLD.meaning: Remove rows narrower than this width (um).
FP_PRUNE_THRESHOLD.symptom: Islets of cells that are hard to connect.

TOP_MARGIN_MULT.meaning: Core-to-die margin as a multiple of the site (relative sizing only).
TOP_MARGIN_MULT.symptom: Only relevant when FP_SIZING is relative.

BOTTOM_MARGIN_MULT.meaning: Core-to-die margin as a multiple of the site (relative sizing only).
BOTTOM_MARGIN_MULT.symptom: Only relevant when FP_SIZING is relative.

LEFT_MARGIN_MULT.meaning: Core-to-die margin as a multiple of the site (relative sizing only).
LEFT_MARGIN_MULT.symptom: Only relevant when FP_SIZING is relative.

RIGHT_MARGIN_MULT.meaning: Core-to-die margin as a multiple of the site (relative sizing only).
RIGHT_MARGIN_MULT.symptom: Only relevant when FP_SIZING is relative.

IO_PIN_PLACEMENT_MODE.symptom: Long I/O wires or congested pin edge.

IO_PIN_MIN_DISTANCE.symptom: 109 Wishbone pins need about 2.3 um pitch on one 250 um edge.

PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT.meaning: Target cell density (percent) of global placement (alias PL_TARGET_DENSITY). Unset means FP_CORE_UTIL + 5 * GPL_CELL_PADDING + 10 (logged as -density in step 28).
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT.safe: Between the design's utilisation + 5 and 95. Below the real utilisation GPL cannot reach the target (GPL-0301).
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT.symptom: Higher: tighter packing, shorter wires, more congestion. Lower: cells spread, longer wires, fewer congestion hot spots. Congestion (GRT-0116) or long wires: try 10 points either way and compare.
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT.verify: 28-openroad-globalplacement log (Placement target density), metrics.json route__wirelength__estimated, design__instance__utilization
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT.repo: unset in all designs (about 0.56 for vision_block)

GPL_CELL_PADDING.meaning: Cell padding (sites) in global placement; also feeds the default density and the heuristic diode inserter.
GPL_CELL_PADDING.symptom: Congestion in dense logic; user_proj_example uses 2 with DPL_CELL_PADDING 2.

DPL_CELL_PADDING.meaning: Cell padding (sites) in detailed placement; must be <= GPL_CELL_PADDING.
DPL_CELL_PADDING.symptom: Detailed-placement legalisation failures or DRC at cell abutments.

PL_ROUTABILITY_DRIVEN.meaning: Congestion-aware global placement (cell inflation in congested tiles).
PL_ROUTABILITY_DRIVEN.symptom: Turning it off is faster but risks GRT congestion.

PL_TIMING_DRIVEN.verify: setup slack in metrics.json; slower flow

PL_WIRE_LENGTH_COEF.meaning: Initial wirelength coefficient; lower tightens wirelength.

PL_ROUTABILITY_OVERFLOW_THRESHOLD.meaning: Overflow at which the routability pass starts.

PL_MIN_PHI_COEFFICIENT.meaning: Lower bound of the GPL mu_k coefficient.
PL_MIN_PHI_COEFFICIENT.safe: Unset; use only if GPL diverges

PL_MAX_PHI_COEFFICIENT.meaning: Upper bound of the GPL mu_k coefficient.
PL_MAX_PHI_COEFFICIENT.safe: Unset; use only if GPL diverges

PL_KEEP_RESIZE_BELOW_OVERFLOW.meaning: With PL_TIMING_DRIVEN: keep resizer changes below this overflow.

PL_MAX_DISPLACEMENT_X.meaning: Max x displacement (um) of a cell in detailed placement.

PL_MAX_DISPLACEMENT_Y.meaning: Max y displacement (um) of a cell in detailed placement.

DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.meaning: Slew margin (percent) of repair_design after global placement (alias PL_RESIZER_MAX_SLEW_MARGIN): tightens the max-transition limit by this percent while repairing.
DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.safe: 20 (default) to 40. The 70 percent used in early tiny_ai_core runs made the repair chase unfixable input-port slews and the 8 GB container ran out of memory; 40 percent also ran out for the 80 and 120 um designs.
DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.symptom: Max-slew violations after repair: raise in steps of 10 and watch memory (resources.json). Container killed in step 32: lower it.
DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.verify: step 32 log, metrics.json design__max_slew_violation__count, resources.json container_peak_mem_gb
DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.repo: 40 for 12 tiny designs, 20 for the 9 larger ones (//SLEW comments); alias spelling in the configs

DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_CAP_PCT.meaning: Capacitance margin (percent) of the post-GPL repair_design (alias PL_RESIZER_MAX_CAP_MARGIN).

DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH.meaning: Max wire length (um) for buffer insertion in repair_design; 0 means no length-based buffering.

DESIGN_REPAIR_BUFFER_INPUT_PORTS.meaning: Buffer every input port during repair.

DESIGN_REPAIR_BUFFER_OUTPUT_PORTS.meaning: Buffer every output port during repair.

DESIGN_REPAIR_TIE_SEPARATION.symptom: Tie cells next to their loads.

PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN.meaning: Setup slack margin (ns) of repair_timing after CTS: repair until slack >= margin. Default 0.05.
PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN.safe: 0 to 0.5 (never negative). prec_* float designs use 0.5, user_proj_example 0.4.
PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN.symptom: Setup slack thin after route: raise the margin to overfix, at the cost of cells.

PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN.meaning: Hold slack margin (ns) of repair_timing after CTS. Default 0.1.
PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN.symptom: Hold slack thin (vision_block min_ff hold is +0.11 ns): raise to overfix; costs delay buffers.

PL_RESIZER_ALLOW_SETUP_VIOS.meaning: Allow hold repair to create setup violations.
PL_RESIZER_ALLOW_SETUP_VIOS.safe: false (BLOCKED to true by the what-if tools: weakens timing)

PL_RESIZER_SETUP_BUFFERING.meaning: Rebuffering / load splitting during setup repair.

PL_RESIZER_SETUP_MAX_BUFFER_PCT.meaning: Max buffers inserted for setup, percent of instances.

PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT.meaning: Max buffers inserted for hold, percent of instances.

PL_RESIZER_SETUP_MAX_UTIL_PCT.meaning: Core utilisation cap during setup repair.

PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_UTIL_PCT.meaning: Core utilisation cap during hold repair.

PL_RESIZER_SETUP_REPAIR_TNS_PCT.meaning: Percent of violating endpoints to repair (setup).

PL_RESIZER_HOLD_REPAIR_TNS_PCT.meaning: Percent of violating endpoints to repair (hold).

RUN_POST_CTS_RESIZER_TIMING.meaning: Run the post-CTS timing repair step.
RUN_POST_CTS_RESIZER_TIMING.safe: true. Switching it off is a way to weaken timing and is BLOCKED.

GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.meaning: Slew margin (percent) of repair_design after global routing (default 10).
GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.safe: 10 to 40; same OOM caveat as the post-GPL margin
GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT.verify: step 41 log; metrics.json design__max_slew_violation__count; resources.json peak memory

GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH.meaning: Max wire length (um) after global routing; 0 means no length-based buffering.

GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_RUN_GRT.meaning: Run global routing before and after the post-GRT repair.

RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR.meaning: Enable the post-GRT design repair step.

RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING.meaning: Enable the post-GRT timing repair step (default off).
RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING.safe: true for the float prec_* designs and user_proj_example
RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING.symptom: Setup/hold still thin after CTS repair.

GRT_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN.meaning: Setup slack margin (ns) after global routing (default 0.025).

GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN.meaning: Hold slack margin (ns) after global routing (default 0.05).

GRT_RESIZER_ALLOW_SETUP_VIOS.meaning: Allow hold repair to create setup violations after routing.

GRT_RESIZER_SETUP_GATE_CLONING.meaning: Gate cloning during post-GRT setup repair.

CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE.meaning: Max flip-flops per sink cluster (one buffer per cluster).
CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE.symptom: Clock skew or too many clock buffers.
CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE.repo: 8 for tiny_ai_core and the soc_* macros (about 420 flops)

CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_MAX_DIAMETER.meaning: Max diameter (um) of a sink cluster.

CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS.meaning: Distance between clock buffers on a clock wire (um).

CTS_CLK_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH.meaning: Max wire length on the clock net (um).

CTS_BALANCE_LEVELS.meaning: Keep similar tree depth across non-register cells.

CTS_APPLY_NDR.meaning: Non-default routing rule on clock nets: none, root_only, half, full.
CTS_APPLY_NDR.symptom: Clock wire resistance vs routing resource.

CTS_ROOT_BUFFER.meaning: Cell inserted at the clock root.

CTS_OBSTRUCTION_AWARE.meaning: Do not place clock buffers on blockages or macros.

RUN_CTS.safe: true. False only in the elaborate-only wrappers (fixed); BLOCKED for macros.

GRT_ADJUSTMENT.meaning: Fraction (0..1) of routing tracks reserved on every layer (default 0.3).
GRT_ADJUSTMENT.safe: 0.1 to 0.5. Raising reserves more space and reduces congestion at the price of longer wires; lowering it to chase a pass is not a fix.
GRT_ADJUSTMENT.symptom: GRT-0116 congestion: raise slightly, but the repo lesson is that congestion is a placement/pin problem (fewer ordered pins, lower density).

GRT_OVERFLOW_ITERS.meaning: Max global-router iterations while overflow remains (default 50).

GRT_ALLOW_CONGESTION.meaning: Continue past congestion. Hides a placement problem; GRT-0116 fixes in this repo were never done with it (kept false).

RT_MAX_LAYER.meaning: Highest routing layer. Macros use met4 so the wrapper can route over them on met5.
RT_MAX_LAYER.safe: met4 for macros. Wrapper: not editable.
RT_MAX_LAYER.symptom: Routing capacity; met5 would block the wrapper's PDN.

RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR.safe: true in macros. Turning it off is BLOCKED (weakens a check); wrappers turn it off (fixed) because a router diode there is unpowered.
RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

DIODE_ON_PORTS.meaning: Always insert diodes on ports of this polarity (none, in, out, both).
DIODE_ON_PORTS.safe: in for tiny_ai_core and soc_* macros; none otherwise
DIODE_ON_PORTS.symptom: Antenna violations on long macro pin wires in the wrapper.
DIODE_ON_PORTS.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION.meaning: Heuristic diode insertion before routing (needs GPL_CELL_PADDING > 0).
RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION.safe: true in 19 designs, false for the three macros with DIODE_ON_PORTS
RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

HEURISTIC_ANTENNA_THRESHOLD.meaning: Manhattan distance (um) above which the heuristic inserter adds a diode.
HEURISTIC_ANTENNA_THRESHOLD.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

GRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_ITERS.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

GRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_MARGIN.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_ITERS.meaning: Max antenna repair iterations in detailed routing.
DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_ITERS.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_MARGIN.meaning: Percent to over-fix antenna violations in DRT.
DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_MARGIN.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

DIODE_PADDING.meaning: Diode cell padding (sites) during placement checks.
DIODE_PADDING.doc: docs/OPENROAD_ENGINES.md section 'ant: antenna checker and repair'

DRT_OPT_ITERS.symptom: DRC left after routing: more iterations; time grows.

DRT_SAVE_SNAPSHOTS.meaning: Save an odb snapshot every routing iteration (large).

DRT_SAVE_DRC_REPORT_ITERS.meaning: Write a DRC report every N iterations.

RUN_FILL_INSERTION.safe: true. False only in the wrappers (fixed).
RUN_FILL_INSERTION.symptom: Fill is needed for density DRC.

RUN_TAP_ENDCAP_INSERTION.safe: true. False only in the wrappers (fixed).

RUN_POST_GPL_DESIGN_REPAIR.meaning: Run the post-GPL design repair step.

RUN_LINTER.safe: true; turning it off is BLOCKED
